chunks: And Saʿd narrated from Abū Jaʿfar, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about qunūt: in which prayers should I perform qunūt? He said: Do not perform qunūt except in the Fajr prayer.

So the proper way regarding these reports is that we understand them to mean that in these prayers qunūt is not on the level of special merit and emphasized recommendation to the extent established in other prayers in which recitation is audible, and after that in the obligatory prayers, because the merit of qunūt in the prayers is graded. Thus, qunūt in the obligatory prayers is more excellent than in the supererogatory prayers, and in those obligatory prayers in which recitation is audible it is more excellent than in those in which it is not audible, and the Maghrib and Fajr prayers, among the audible prayers, are more strongly emphasized in this regard.

And when we interpret the reports according to these aspects, a sound basis is established for each of them that does not conflict with the others. It is also possible that they only negated qunūt in some prayers and specified it in others as a form of taqiyyah and practical consideration, because among the generality there are those who hold that view, and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation or precautionary practice due to circumstances
key_terms.النَّدْبِ: recommended status, as opposed to obligation
key_terms.الْفَجْرِ: the Fajr prayer, singled out in the narration
key_terms.الْفَضْلِ: special merit or superiority in reward
key_terms.الْقُنُوتِ: the supplicatory devotion performed in prayer at the designated place

ai.seo_question: In which prayers is qunūt performed, and how are the differing hadith about it reconciled?
ai.summary: This text discusses the rulings and relative merit of qunūt in the daily prayers. It explains that reports limiting qunūt to Fajr may be understood as referring to stronger emphasis and greater merit, especially in obligatory and audible prayers, while also allowing for the possibility that some narrations reflect taqiyyah.
